title: The White House announces the Board of Peace and the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza
body:
On 14 January 2026, US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff announced the second phase of the Gaza plan, which he said would move from a ceasefire to demilitarization, technocratic governance and reconstruction. On 16 January the White House announced the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG) and a Board of Peace. The NCAG, led by Dr. Ali Shaath, a Gaza-born technocrat who has worked with the Palestinian Authority, first met in Cairo on 15 January. The Times of Israel reported it had 15 members, with expected portfolios including agriculture, trade, health, education, police and security.

The Board of Peace is chaired by President Donald Trump, and its initial eight members include Marco Rubio, Steve Witkoff, Tony Blair, Nickolay Mladenov and Jared Kushner. Mladenov was also named to head the Office of the High Representative in Gaza. A Gaza Executive Board with 11 initial members includes Turkey's Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, Egyptian General Hassan Rashad and members from the United Arab Emirates and Qatar.

Major General Jasper Jeffers was appointed to lead the International Stabilization Force, although it was unclear which countries would contribute troops. According to the Long War Journal, the Israel Defense Forces controlled about half of Gaza during the first phase, with Hamas controlling most of the rest, and one deceased Israeli hostage remained in Gaza. Witkoff warned Hamas of serious consequences if the body was not returned. The Jerusalem Post reported a UN estimate that clearing rubble could take seven years.
